newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed mixed to higher in a slow Monday session which drew some inspiration from U.S. Treasuries, but was dominated by professional arbitrage in the long 2023 bond.
"The long bond is traded by securities houses because it's the most volatile, but I can't make a fundamental story out of it," one trader said.

A second dealer said that professionals were trading the curve against the 10-year guilder benchmark as the spread was at historical highs of 75 basis points. However, another called the spread "fair".

The 6.25 percent 1998 bond also stood out as well traded, sought by those looking for higher returns than in the money market. It also gained on switches out of medium-term maturities on uncertainty over official German and Dutch interest rates.
"It's a safe bond to hide in. Bid/offer spreads are small and well traded. You can get out if you want," a dealer said.
"(German) M3 data were exactly as expected, which was more of a reason to sell than to buy. Also Germany has made pretty clear there's not much room to cut key rates," another said.
Technically the picture looked mixed, with some indicating that support levels had proven solid.
But other dealers pointed at low volumes in bund futures and the fact that the present cycle had reached a top.
Under any circumstances, dealers said Dutch paper could outperform their German counterparts because it was scantily available, especially 10-year paper.
Because of its low borrowing requirement, the Dutch Finance Ministry was not issuing a fourth quarter loan, and the third quarter loan was an unusual 2002 bond.
